answer: Plant traps in the water. Most tasks reward the obvious answer; occasionally the ledger plants one where that answer is wrong — surface pattern pointing one way, truth the other. Genuine evaluators notice; pattern-matchers trained on volume fall in at measurable, recorded rates. A farm’s thousand wallets, optimized for the ocean of easy wins, fail the island of traps together and identically — itself the signal. Real judgment is saffron: specific, rare, harvested by hand. Traps are cheap to plant and impossible to farm around, because you cannot know which questions are traps.
